title: Half-done & All-done: かけ, 切る, 切れない, きり, っぱなし
description: Half-finished (〜かけ), doing completely (〜切る), too much to finish (〜切れない), only / since (きり), and leaving something on (〜っぱなし).

points.title: 〜かけ: half-done, in the middle of
points.summary: ます-stem + かけ(の + noun) = started but not finished: 読みかけの本, 食べかけのパン.
points.body:
- 読み**かけ**の本 (a half-read book).
- 食べ**かけ**のパン.
- 言い**かけ**てやめた (started to say something and stopped) — verb form 〜かける.
examples: {読|よ}みかけの{本|ほん}が{机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}にある。
There's a half-read book on the desk.

points.title: 〜切る: do completely, all the way
points.summary: ます-stem + 切る = finish completely, use up: 読み切る, 使い切る, 走り切る.
points.body:
- この本を一晩で読み**切った** (read the whole book in one night).
- お金を使い**切った** (used up all the money).

切る is godan: 切ります, 切った, 切って.
examples: お{金|かね}を{全部|ぜんぶ}{使|つか}い{切|き}った。
I used up all the money.

points.title: 〜切れない: too many/much to (finish)
points.summary: ます-stem + 切れない = can't do completely (there's too much): 数え切れない, 食べ切れない.
points.body:
- 星が多すぎて、数え**切れない** (too many to count).
- 一人では食べ**切れない**よ.

Potential negative of 切る.
examples: {星|ほし}が{多|おお}すぎて、{数|かぞ}え{切|き}れない。
There are too many stars to count.

points.title: 〜きり: only, just; since (and nothing after)
points.summary: Noun + きり = only (二人きり). た-form + きり = since … (and then nothing more).
points.body:
- 二人**きり**で話したい (just the two of us).
- 彼は朝出かけた**きり**、まだ帰ってこない (left this morning and hasn't been back since).

Casual: っきり (一人っきり).
examples: {二人|ふたり}きりで{話|はな}したい。
I want to talk, just the two of us.

points.title: 〜っぱなし: leave (something) on / as is
points.summary: ます-stem + っぱなし = leave something in a state (usually carelessly): 開けっぱなし, つけっぱなし.
points.body:
- 窓を開け**っぱなし**にしないでください (don't leave the window open).
- テレビをつけ**っぱなし**で寝てしまった.

Usually negative (careless). Also 'continuously': 立ちっぱなし (standing the whole time).
examples: テレビをつけっぱなしで{寝|ね}てしまった。
I fell asleep with the TV left on.

questions.prompt: {読|よ}み（　）の{本|ほん}が{机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}にある。
notes: かけるの本 isn't grammatical.
かけての本 isn't grammatical.
かけたの本 isn't grammatical.
questions.translation: There's a half-read book on the desk.

questions.prompt: {食|た}べ（　）のパンを{捨|す}てないで。
notes: 切るの isn't grammatical.
食べきり isn't used here.
食べっぱなし = 'leaving it after eating' — not 'half-eaten'.
questions.translation: Don't throw away the half-eaten bread.

questions.prompt: この{本|ほん}を{一晩|ひとばん}で{読|よ}み（　）。
questions.explanation: Read completely: 読み**切った** (godan past).
notes: The dictionary form doesn't fit the past context.
The て-form can't end the sentence.
切る is godan: 切った, not 切りた.
questions.translation: I read this whole book in one night.

questions.prompt: What does 「お{金|かね}を{使|つか}い{切|き}った」 mean?
options: I used up all the money.
notes: 切る as a helper means 'completely', not 'cut'.
That would be 使えなかった.
That would be 少し使った.

questions.prompt: {星|ほし}が{多|おお}すぎて、{数|かぞ}え（　）。
questions.explanation: Too many to finish counting: **切れない**.
notes: 切らない = 'won't do completely' — not 'can't'.
切れる = 'can do completely' — contradicts 多すぎて.
切った = 'counted them all' — contradicts 多すぎて.
questions.translation: There are too many stars to count.

questions.prompt: こんなにたくさん、{一人|ひとり}では{食|た}べ（　）よ。
notes: 切らない = 'won't finish'.
切り can't end the sentence before よ.
切った = 'finished it all'.
questions.translation: I can't eat this much on my own.

questions.prompt: {誰|だれ}にも{聞|き}かれたくないので、{二人|ふたり}（　）で{話|はな}したい。
questions.explanation: Just the two of us: **二人きり**.
notes: 二人っぱなし isn't a word.
二人ぎみ isn't a word.
二人かけ isn't a word.
questions.translation: I don't want anyone to hear, so I want to talk with just the two of us.

questions.prompt: {彼|かれ}は{朝|あさ}{出|で}かけた（　）、まだ{帰|かえ}ってこない。
notes: ぎみ doesn't attach to the た-form.
っぱなし attaches to the ます-stem, not the た-form.
出かけたかけ isn't grammatical.
questions.translation: He left this morning and hasn't been back since.

questions.prompt: {窓|まど}を{開|あ}け（　）にしないでください。
notes: 開け切り isn't natural here.
開けきりにする isn't natural.
開けかけにする isn't natural.
questions.translation: Please don't leave the window open.

questions.prompt: テレビをつけ（　）で{寝|ね}てしまった。
notes: つけぎみ isn't a word.
つけきり isn't natural.
つけかけ = 'about to switch it on' — doesn't fit falling asleep with it on.
questions.translation: I fell asleep with the TV left on.

notes: っぱなして isn't a form.
言いきって = 'said it outright' — contradicts やめた.
言いかかって isn't a word.
questions.translation: She started to say something, then stopped.

questions.prompt: マラソンを{最後|さいご}まで{走|はし}り（　）。
questions.explanation: Ran all the way: **走り切った**.
notes: 切て isn't a form.
切れった isn't a form.
切る is godan: 切った.
questions.translation: I ran the marathon all the way to the end.

questions.prompt: {一日中|いちにちじゅう}{立|た}ち（　）で{疲|つか}れた。
questions.explanation: Continuously (the whole time): **立ちっぱなし**.
notes: 立ちぎみ isn't a word.
立ちかけ = 'about to stand'.
立ちきり isn't natural.
questions.translation: I was on my feet all day and I'm exhausted.
